newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says will keep flying Airbuses.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says will keep flying Airbuses.

text.p: National flag carrier Garuda Indonesia intends to continue flying its six Airbus Industrie A330-300 aircraft despite concerns by other carriers about their Rolls-Royce Trent 700 engines.
"What I can tell you is our aircraft are still flying. So far we haven't had any problems," Garuda spokesman Arief Hartanto told Reuters.

Hong Kong airlines Cathay Pacific and Dragonair said on Saturday they had suspended operations of their total 15 Airbus A330-300 aircraft due to concerns about the reliability of their Rolls-Royce Trent 700 engines.
Both cancelled flights on Saturday as a result.
Rolls-Royce said on Friday it had identified the problem with the engines and was working with its customers to solve it.
A series of Trent 700 engine failures on A330 aircraft of the two Hong Kong airlines in recent weeks has forced the twin-engined planes to make emergency landings on one engine.

The latest was a Dragonair A330 which made an emergency landing at the Philippines' Subic Bay on Friday after developing engine trouble en route from Hong Kong to Malaysia's Kota Kinabalu. Hartanto referred further enquiries to the Jakarta office of Rolls-Royce which was closed on Saturday.
